column2: if it’s a planeswalker and another planeswalker with the same subtype is controlled by the same player
column3: Outdated in part: dated 2013-07-01, when the planeswalker uniqueness rule was in force (704.5j in the CR effective 2017-08-25: “If a player controls two or more planeswalkers that share a planeswalker type, that player chooses one of them, and the rest are put into their owners’ graveyards. This is called the “planeswalker uniqueness rule.””); the CR effective 2017-09-29 (Ixalan) removed it (306.4 there: “Previously, planeswalkers were subject to a “planeswalker uniqueness rule” that stopped a player from controlling two planeswalkers of the same planeswalker type. This rule has been removed”; archived CR texts). Two planeswalkers with the same subtype both stay (tests/rulings/r_residue_misc_1_leaves.rs, two_planeswalkers_with_the_same_subtype_both_stay). The ruling's other reasons still hold and stay cited (indestructible_permanents_still_go_to_the_graveyard_other_ways); logged in docs/RULING_DISCREPANCIES.md
